existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Labrousse’s serial prices and incomes connect economic conjunctures with social structures
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Braudel, p. 729, discusses price, wage, and demographic series; Gurevich identifies quantitative inquiry among Annales approaches. This does not derive econometric cliometrics or all historical demography from Annales. The 1933 title is now checked; this remains a specific French serial contribution, not the source of every form of quantitative history.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.map_label: Labrousse: serial prices, incomes and social structure

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Contributes conjunctural evidence and questions about uneven social crises
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: The primary 1956 opening differentiates sectors; Grenier/Lepetit’s later abstract distinguishes Labrousse’s experimental intentions from a narrowed serial reception. Neither source makes his programme the whole of Annales.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Labrousse’s conjunctures and social inquiry serve as explicit examples in Braudel’s temporal argument
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Braudel names the 1933 study, revolutionary-crisis inquiry and 1955 collective programme. Praise coexists with reservations about a return toward short duration; social and economic rhythms need not coincide. The graph dates La Crise to 1944 using separate bibliographic evidence.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Simiand’s serial analysis is a named antecedent of Labrousse’s economic method
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: The scholarly obituary names Simiand and Hamilton. This group-level arrow concerns Simiand specifically, not direct personal transmission from Durkheim, and the retrospective attribution is narrower than Labrousse’s own testimony.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Labrousse supervises Perrot’s strike research, which adapts serial training to workers’ lives
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Lacoue-Labarthe’s scholarly biography identifies thesis supervision and statistical training alongside voices and gestures. This names one formation and selective adaptation; Perrot’s later feminist programme is not reduced to this connection.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Later economic historians question the crisis model’s conditions and its narrowed serial reception
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Grenier/Lepetit’s abstract distinguishes original experimental intentions from reception. Simonin’s opening reports causal objections and attempts a conditional defense. Different positions coexist; unread derivations and primary critics are not claimed independently checked.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Perrot: serial training and strike histories
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Retrospective biographical evidence documents supervision and a particular adaptation; Perrot’s later feminist work is not reduced to this training.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.map_label: Perrot: serial training and strike histories

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Labrousse's price and conjuncture history as a model for Ouellet's economic and social history of Quebec, as Ouellet acknowledged (per Savard) and his critics named it
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: In-period readers; Ouellet's own acknowledgement is reported, not read. Savard (1974, ¶8, read): 'Ouellet a dit sa dette envers les travaux exemplaires de Labrousse et de Chaunu'. Paquet and Wallot (1972, read) call him 'un tenant de la position Labrousse' (p. 187) and contrast the 'position Labrousse', for which agriculture is the leading sector, with their own 'position Mauro-North' (pp. 187, 235). Tousignant (1980, p. 416) describes his method as quantitative series combined with a Weberian typology of mentalities, without naming Labrousse. The 1966 book's subtitle, 'structures et conjoncture', and Mandrou's preface are recorded on qcreq_ouellet_1966; the book is unread. Ouellet's 1985 survey (p. 47) describes 'L'histoire sociale à la façon de Labrousse' as one Annales tendency but does not there speak of his own debt.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Corbin explains his departure from Labrousse’s economic-to-mentalities model when subsistence practices and unreliable statistics frustrated his study of the Limousin.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own interview given in 2003, read in Christian Pierre Kasper’s 2005 Portuguese translation, pp. 14–15. Corbin describes abandoning much of the model, not every quantitative method or all of Labrousse’s work. Bertrand Gille, whom Labrousse recommended, was his actual supervisor and helped prompt the methodological change; Labrousse is not silently substituted for Gille.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Prost criticizes the Labroussian paradigm’s ready-made classes, explanatory reductions and restricted room for agency.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: The argument also recognizes its economic explanatory gains and says the agency problem is not exclusive to Labrousse or Marxist historians. It defends historically reconstructed classes, rather than abandoning social history. Selected authorial passage in the expanded digital edition, identified by EPUB ISBN 9782757843765 (BAnQ catalog: April 2014). Read through a public third-party transcription, not a collated print facsimile. No claim that the exact wording was present in 1996; complete book and cited originals unread.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Charle names Labrousse among the economic readings that helped him understand publishing, imperial societies, theatre and spectacle.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own 2015 retrospective 78, economic-reading paragraph: this is one credited resource within two expressly plural lists, not a sole model, unique concept attribution or claim to economic-history specialization. Simiand, Vilar, Bouvier, Verley and the other named Marxist and regulation writers retain separate credit. Original works and individual transfers beyond the author’s stated uses were not freshly read. The public web-tool PDF extract was checked; direct current publisher-file retrieval returned 404, so no local complete PDF or later interview pages are claimed read.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Roche credits Labrousse’s contextual political history and advice to avoid another regional or urban monograph in shaping his research choices.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own recollection161–163 explicitly identifies him as a pupil and describes the advice. Alphonse Dupront separately accepted supervision of Roche’s self-devised academy thesis. No sole-supervisor claim; political contexts are not reduced to a food-crisis cause.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Vovelle identifies Labrousse as the teacher who taught him historical and archival research within a social-history framework.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own 2005 answers 2–3 and 17 explicitly identify Labrousse as his master and explain the passage through economic, conjunctural and social history. Tersen’s referral and the broader Marxist setting retain separate credit. Vovelle subsequently took distance from limits of this framework while keeping social history; no claim of total doctrinal obedience or later individual influence from Simiand simply because a comparison is invoked.

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: Pirenne’s comparative economic history and Labrousse’s study of economic conjunctures contribute to different parts of Annales
named_group_routes_inspected.evidence_note: The original journal title and Gurevich’s methodological account support economic history as a constituent of the project. This is a field-level contribution, not the claim that one later economic-history school founded Annales.
named_group_routes_inspected.map_label: Pirenne and Labrousse: distinct economic histories

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: Labroussian economic and social history at Laval
named_group_routes_inspected.evidence_note: Savard (1974) says Ouellet owed a debt to Labrousse and Chaunu; Robert Mandrou prefaced Ouellet’s 1966 book (review heading). Dechêne trained in France in the Annales milieu of Mandrou and Goubert before her Paris doctorate (1973), published as Habitants et marchands (1974) (Charron, Dictionnaire universel des créatrices; formal supervision not asserted). Linteau (1983) says social history began in Quebec in the 1960s under Annales influence but that his generation was shaped more by French and Quebec sociologists and American historians. Specific contributions to the Laval and New France strands, not an Annales origin for Quebec historiography.

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: An agricultural crisis from 1802, joined to population pressure and a peasantry slow to change its methods, as the ground of French-Canadian nationalism and, in large part, of the 1837–38 rebellion (1962–76)
named_group_routes_inspected.evidence_note: In-period, his own texts. With Jean Hamelin (1962, read in full): 'la détérioration rapide de l'agriculture bas-canadienne après 1802 prouve le caractère superficiel des conquêtes antérieures. Dès le début du 19e siècle, la tendance majeure se renverse' (p. 20); 'la routine paysanne, la pauvreté des moyens de transport, les habitudes de consommation de l'habitant canadien-français et l'incompréhension des politiciens expliquent la lenteur des départs et des progrès'; 'Aussi la révolution de 1837-38 apparaît-elle, en grande partie, comme une réponse détournée aux problèmes posés par l'action conjointe des tensions démographiques et de la crise agricole' (p. 31); the crisis reveals 'deux entités culturelles sans aucun doute distinctes mais offrant une grande disparité dans leur degré d'évolution', so that 'c'est moins la diversité des valeurs que la différence des niveaux d'évolution qui fut la source fondamentale des conflits raciaux'; qualification: 'Ce n'est pas que cette crise soit le seul moteur des événements de cette époque troublée' (p. 32). His 1976 restatement (read in full): the habitant, 'un paysan traditionnel', adapted positively to the export market from 1760 to 1802 (p. 115); thereafter 'le paysan, au lieu de transformer ses façons de faire, se durcit et résiste aux pressions en faveur de la rénovation du système agricole'; nationalism was born 'parmi les professions libérales' and spread 'dans les milieux paysans sous l'effet de l'apparition du problème agricole et des pressions démographiques' (p. 116). His books as quoted by critics (unread here): Paquet and Wallot (1972, pp. 193–194) quote the 1966 Histoire (p. 184) that 'l'explication ultime dans la diminution des exportations de céréales réside ... dans une défaillance de la production locale', and his 1964 CHR article (p. 291) that 'la crise agricole, par ses nombreuses implications, serait donc la toile de fond de l'aventure nationaliste'. In-period readers: Paquet and Wallot (1972, p. 187): 'pour un tenant de la position Labrousse comme F. Ouellet, la "crise agricole" est le pivot de toute l'interprétation socio-économique de l'histoire du Bas-Canada au tournant du XIXe siècle'; Savard (1974, ¶8): 'Ouellet a dit sa dette envers les travaux exemplaires de Labrousse et de Chaunu'; Bouchard (1990, ¶13): 'Dans la foulée de Fernand Ouellet et de Jean Hamelin qui, avec quelques autres, ont introduit ici l'histoire sociale, toute une génération d'historiens entreprit alors une nouvelle lecture du passé québécois'. A contribution to the Laval strand and the crisis debate, not a founding; the critics are on edge 2.

named_group_routes_inspected.relationship: Using Braudel’s remarks as reported by Dosse, Prost criticizes the marginal place that determinist social history leaves for human agency.
named_group_routes_inspected.evidence_note: Specifically attributed criticism of the determinist rhetoric quoted in this passage, not a general rejection of Braudel. Prost explicitly says the problem extends beyond Labrousse and Marxist historians. Dosse is the named mediator; Braudel’s underlying statements and Dosse’s complete work were not freshly read. Prost’s separate use of Braudel’s warning about retrospective hindsight does not erase this objection. Selected authorial passage in the expanded digital edition, identified by EPUB ISBN 9782757843765 (BAnQ catalog: April 2014). Read through a public third-party transcription, not a collated print facsimile. No claim that the exact wording was present in 1996; complete book and cited originals unread.
